newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo, Croatia agree social insurance accord-agency.
newsitem.headline: Yugo, Croatia agree social insurance accord-agency.

text.p: Yugoslavia and Croatia on Thursday agreed on the text for a bilateral agreement on social insurance, state news agency Tanjug reported.

Yugoslav Deputy Labour and Social Insurance Minister Maksim Korac and his Croatian counterpart Vera Babic said the accord was an important step towards implementation of the agreement on normalisation of bilateral relations, Tanjug reported.
"The agreement will allow citizens of both countries to accomplish their rights based on the social, pension and disability insurance and in the case of unemployment," Babic was quoted as saying.
Korac said the text of the accord is based on the principles valid in European Union countries in the field.
"Nobody's years of service and pension will be put in question," Korac said and added the two delegations did not discuss "citizenship or any other affiliation" during their three-day talks.
He said late payments will be paid out in six months from the moment the agreement on payment operations between Yugoslavia and Croatia comes into force.
The text of the agreement is yet to be verified by the governments and parliaments of Yugoslavia and Croatia.

Yugoslavia and Croatia signed an agreement in August 1996 to normalise relations, severed in 1991, when Croatia declared independance from the former Yugoslav federation. -- Zorana Vucicevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
